text: Fire Hawk Hatchlings are fire hawks located in the Molten Front.

Finishing Reagents are optional crafting reagents that can be used to boost crafting stats while crafting an item. The reagent is consumed on use. For a list of finishing reagents, see :Category:Finishing crafting reagent items.
__NOTOC__ Firava the Rekindler is a fire revenant located in Life-Binder Conservatory in the Waking Shores.

The Finespindle are a family of gnomes that appear to excel in leather crafting. The known members can be found in Ironforge.

__NOTOC__ Firefin Snapper is obtained by fishing and is a component in Fire Oil (made with Alchemy). Fishing for Firefin Snapper requires (fourth tier) fishing skill-level of 130 (or 225 to ensure a catch). Firefin Snapper can be fished straight from the water or also from an Oil Spill School.
Firebloom is an herb that can be gathered with Herbalism (205). Firebloom grows in particularly hot southern areas of Tanaris and is used by the ogres there to spice up their otherwise bland meals.
Firemaw is the fourth boss in Blackwing Lair, found patrolling the Crimson Laboratories after Broodlord Lashlayer and before Ebonroc. He may drop Tier 2 gloves for all classes.
Firewalkers are fire elementals found in Baron Geddon and Shazzrah's room of Molten Core. They spawn linked with one Flameguard and either two Lava Elementals or a Lava Reaver as part of a Lava Pack.

The Firelands (referred to as the Elemental Plane of Fire or just Plane of Fire) is one of the four interlinked domains within the Elemental Plane. It was created eons ago by the titan-forged for the purpose of imprisoning most of Azeroth's fire elementals.

The Firestone was a warlock-only temporary weapon enchants akin to wizard oils and created by the Create Firestone spell. A Firestone increased all spell direct damage done by 1% and increased spell critical strike by 7/14/21/28/35/42/49. They were bind on pickup, but unlike other Conjured Items, Firestones and Spellstones did not vanish after logged out for any amount of time (Much like a Wizard Oil created by Enchanting). Firestones and Spellstones were the preferred temporary weapon enchants for Warlocks. Firestones were preferred for Warlocks that favor direct damage spells (Destruction and Demonology warlocks), while Spellstones were preferred for Affliction Warlocks, who favor damage o

Firewatch Ridge is where the main campsite of the Dark Iron dwarves in Searing Gorge lies. It overlooks the great excavation site of the Cauldron. Dark Irons, their mechanical golems, and giant flame spiders cover most of the ridge, making it exceptionally dangerous for adventurers. The northwestern part of it contains a Twilight's Hammer cave, where you could find elites.

Fireguard Shoulders are leather shoulder armor with a large amount of stamina and fire resistance. These are geared towards rogues and druids but will benefit any class that can wear leather and needs the fire resistance.
Fireproof Cloak is second only to Wildfire Cape for the most Fire Resistance on cloak on a pre-BC item. However, this cloak has additional stats whereas the other cape has none.
The Firetree tribe was one of the forest troll tribes that joined Rend Blackhand after the Second War as part of the Dark Horde.

.]] Fireworks are pyrotechnic devices used primarily for aesthetic and entertainment purposes. They generally produce an in-game animated firework display and/or noise, but usually both. Fireworks are very often used to celebrate special occasions, such as seasonal events.

Firewing Couriers are messengers from one of Kael'thas's strongholds, Firewing Point. They are allied with the Broken and Lost Ones found in Tuurem in Terokkar Forest. These messengers receive and distribute information between the two settlements on plans for attacking the Cenarion Expedition.
Firebrand Dreadweavers are orc spellcastes located in Blackrock Spire.
Firjus the Soul Crusher is a vrykul gladiator in the Ring of Judgement in the Howling Fjord. He needs to be slain during Stunning Defeat at the Ring.
The First Days are described as a time when demons roamed the land. Great heroes had to drive them out of Azeroth and into the Great Dark Beyond.
The First Burning Blade Pyre can be found in the Burning Blade Ruins of Nagrand.

The First Legion Forward Camp is located south of the Bombardment in Icecrown. The camp is a former base of Arthas and his men of the 1st Legion, prior to his corruption. This base may be the first time he openly fought and killed his own men. The Forward Camp was a small base, consisting of a unit of Lordaeron Footsoldiers, their captain and several ballistae.

__NOTOC__ The Firelands Hatchery is a grotto in the Firelands where Sethria smuggled stolen eggs from Mount Hyjal to hatch her own hideous creations of birds of prey trained for war. This area can only be accessed through the flamegate in the Flamewake. Farden Talonshrike can be found at the top near the ledge with Aviana's Guardians. He makes sure to gather all the noble guardians and get them out of the cavern before it collapses on itself. Numa Skyclaw can be found at the bottom retrieving the fallen guardians.

The First Bank of Kezan is a heavily-fortified bank of Bilgewater Port in Kezan. Unlike other banks, it deals in macaroons, a form of goblin paper money. Here, a long line of Kezan Citizens wait to deal with two FBoK Bank Tellers. There are First Bank of Kezan Vaults.
Firehawk Mariners are blood elves found on The Firehawk on the waters of The Sea Reaver's Run, south of Hrothgar's Landing.

in the Firelands.]] The Firelands Invasion is a charge led by Malfurion Stormrage and the Guardians of Hyjal to take the attack to Ragnaros in the Firelands. A new currency, Mark of the World Tree, is introduced. Marks are rewarded from completing daily quests and can be used to unlock the Molten Front, areas within it, and purchase high-level items at the following vendors: Zen'Vorka, Ayla Shadowstorm, Varlan Highbough and Damek Bloombeard. The progression of the storyline is tracked in the achievement The Molten Front Offensive.
The Fireheart Necklace is sold for by Zen'Vorka inside the Sentinel Tree of Malfurion's Breach on the Molten Front.

Firekin are level 85 creatures that appear from fire portals to guard from wisps in the Molten Front, during the quest Wisp Away. They look like red grells and will initially try to kill the wisps by casting fireballs on them, until they're killed or change aggro towards something else. They spawn rapidly, but are easily killed due to their low health. Only 8 firekin (which have to be killed) will spawn each time you do the quest.

Fireplume Peak is a volcano in the northwestern most part of the Molten Front in the Firelands. It's here that fire hawks make their home. The Fire Hawk Matriarch and her eggs can be found at the top, while lava elementals roam around the base. If players are lucky, they can catch a glimpse of the diamond crab, Karkin, and the gemmed ocelot, Skarr, since they're often found on the pathway of floating rocks.

Firegut Furnace is an ogre mound at the base of Dreadmaul Rock in the Burning Steppes. The Firegut Ogres make their home here. Since their alliance with the Blackrock clan, the Furnace is occasionally visited by high-ranking Blackrock orcs.

First Sergeant is a player vs. player achievement earned for getting an 1500 rating in rated battlegrounds.

First Lieutenant Wiley is the second in command of the Alliance forces in the Darkbreak Cove. He and Captain Glovaal command the Pincer X2 submarine when it transports adventurers from the surface to Darkbreak Cove. He is not known to be involved in the subsequent battle against the naga in the Abyssal Depths.

First Lieutenant Pieracci is the second in command of the Horde forces in the Tenebrous Cavern. He and Captain "Jewels" Verne command the Verne submarine when it transports adventurers from the surface to Tenebrous Cavern. He is not known to be involved in the subsequent battle against the naga in the Abyssal Depths.

Firewalkers' Path starts at immediately to the east of Old Pi'jiu on the southern side of the Timeless Isle, then heads eastward through the Firewalker Ruins, turns northeast over the Croaking Hollow, past the Blazing Way and the Shrine of the Black Flame, then switches back westward to cross over the Red Stone Run before turning north and stopping at at the broken span before the Ordon Sanctuary.
The Firewalker Ruins are on the first rise of the Firewalkers' Path on the southeastern side of Timeless Isle. The ruins are above the Red Stone Run to the north and the Croaking Hollow to the east.
Firestorm Eggs are found in out-of-the-way areas wherever Crimsonscale Firestorms can be found, generally on the Firewalkers' Path and the Blazing Way on the eastern side of the Timeless Isle.
Firetotem Bracers are a possible drop from Ordos, the world boss yaungol on the Timeless Isle.

The First Age of Creation was an age named by the Titans on ancient Azeroth mentioned by Highlord Demitrian. According to him, the elementals ruled Azeroth before that time. The Elemental Sundering, occurred some time after this age. The Titans, ruled by an elite sect known as the Pantheon, brought order to a hundred million worlds scattered throughout the Great Dark Beyond during the first ages of creation. It may be also referred to as age of the Titans. Long after it, the Age of a Hundred Kings began.

Firim (formerly Al'firim) is an eccentric broker encountered in Zereth Mortis. He was originally a member of Cartel Al and led an expedition to search for the Sepulcher of the First Ones, a mission that ended with his disappearance and the other brokers labeling him a madman and heretic. In reality, his expedition succeeded in reaching Zereth Mortis, the land of the First Ones, but once there Firim was turned into a pariah again: his colleagues renamed themselves the Enlightened and declared him an apostate for wanting to continue to study the mysteries of the First Ones instead of simply revering them, eventually leading them to banish him from their town of Haven. The First Forgelite was a kyrian who served as the first Forgelite Prime of Bastion. She wielded the hammer :Phaestus, Genesis of Aeons, and was responsible for the creation of the first centurions and the Spires of Ascension, as well as the design of the Mnemonic Locus. According to Mikanikos, she was a prolific soul who "recorded everything". It's not stated what happened to her, but she was succeeded as Forgelite Prime by Mikanikos, who has held the title ever since. The Eternal Forge contains a shrine to the First Forgelite.

.]] Fishing is a secondary profession. It allows adventurers to fish various objects, primarily fish and other waterbound creatures, from water, lava and even liquid mercury. Fist weapons are those which are gripped in a fist, such as brass knuckles. Due to the small number of fist weapons in the game they can make a poor choice of weaponry before level 60. However, if you know where to look and are willing to put some extra time into running dungeons you should be able to find enough upgrades that this won't be a problem. The class proficiencies page lists which classes can use this type of weapon.

This page details fish, one of the six main types of food in WoW. Fish is the edible flesh of a fish or other aquatic animals, not necessarily fish in a biological sense. Most of these are represented as a single fish inventory item that stacks in twenties, as does most other food. Some aquatic or semi-aquatic animals, such as crocolisks drop meat, representing their flesh, not fish. Also, aquatic means dwells in water, but in WoW, some fish can be fished from other liquid environments, lava in particular. Not all fish are edible. Fishing Pole refers to the basic starting fishing pole with no fishing skill nor level requirement to equip, and no bonus to fishing skill. You can purchase it and wield it as a melee weapon with no fishing training, but you cannot fish with it until you train in Apprentice Fishing. All characters will begin fishing using this item.

Fixed device, or fixed object is a not widely used term that applies to any object that cannot be picked up or moved (is fixed in place) in the game world, but can be interacted with in some way (buys from your character, works like a container, exchanges items, opens or closes, gives a quest, can be read, repairs your items, sells to a character, etc.). The most commonly used object of this type is the mailbox. Fixed devices are distinguished from spawned objects in that they never appear based on some trigger or disappear after use. They are always present in the game world. ;Examples of fixed devices: * Mailboxes, forges, anvils and permanent cooking fires * In-game books * Doors and leve
